title: Low-trust ingestion is isolated from privileged capability
summary: Workloads that ingest untrusted content run in a separate profile without broad credentials or admin toolsets.

protected.asset: Credentials, private data and admin surfaces of the wider deployment
protected.failure: Hostile ingested content obtains privileged credentials or administrative tool access in the same session.

rationale: Untrusted input plus private data plus outward capability is the canonical dangerous intersection. Separating ingestion into its own bounded profile removes an edge from that triangle: the ingestion profile gets only the toolsets and credential scopes its job needs, and no administrative reach.

variants.description: A dedicated ingestion profile with a minimal toolset, no memory-write capability and credentials scoped to its purpose.
Ingestion runs on a separate container or host with its own network position and no route to privileged surfaces.

verification.method: Inventory the ingestion profile's effective toolsets, credential scopes by name only, and network reach toward privileged surfaces; attempt a denied privileged call where a disposable target exists.
verification.evidence: Toolset and credential-scope inventory by name, plus denial outcomes; no credential values.

rollback.method: Merge or remove the separated profile only with an explicit owner decision recorded, since rollback here widens the trust boundary.

failure_modes: The ingestion profile keeps one broad administrative credential 'temporarily'.
A globally enabled extension silently re-adds privileged tools to every profile.
Network isolation is assumed from the profile name without testing reachability.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
